title: Submit URLs to Bing with IndexNow
description: A complete setup guide for the IndexNow key file, request payload, validation, and safe retry behavior.
summary: Set up a key file, prepare a single-host URL batch, submit it, and diagnose the response.

sections.title: What IndexNow does
paragraphs: IndexNow lets a site notify participating search engines when a URL is added, updated, or deleted. It is a discovery signal, not a guarantee that the URL will be crawled or indexed.
A single request may contain up to 10,000 URLs. Every URL in that request must use the same hostname as the host field.

items.title: Generate a key
items.description: Use an 8–128 character key containing letters, numbers, and hyphens.

items.title: Publish the key file
items.description: Serve a plain UTF-8 text file whose body contains only the key. The default path is https://host/key.txt.

items.title: Verify it publicly
items.description: Check the final response outside your authenticated session and confirm that redirects stay on the submitted host.

sections.title: Submit and interpret the response
paragraphs: Normalize and deduplicate the URL list before sending it. Treat 200 and 202 as successful receipt, fix 400/403/422 before retrying, and back off when the endpoint returns 429.

sections.title: Reference JSON request
paragraphs: Every batch request posts UTF-8 JSON to an IndexNow endpoint such as https://www.bing.com/indexnow or https://api.indexnow.org/indexnow. Submitting to one participating endpoint automatically shares the notification across Bing, Yandex, Seznam, Naver, and other IndexNow partners.

items.title: Exact hostname match
items.description: Keep apex (example.com) and www (www.example.com) in separate requests with matching keyLocation hosts.

items.title: Canonical URLs only
items.description: Strip UTM tracking parameters, URL fragments (#section), and duplicate trailing-slash variants before submitting.

items.title: Delta-only cadence
items.description: Submit only newly published, updated, or deleted URLs rather than re-submitting your full sitemap on every deploy.

title: IndexNow 200: OK
description: What an IndexNow HTTP 200 response means and what to verify after a successful request.
summary: The request was accepted and the key was validated.

sections.title: Meaning
paragraphs: The endpoint accepted the request and validated its shape and ownership key. This confirms receipt, not indexing.

items.title: Record the batch
items.description: Keep only the host, URL count, time, and status needed for operational history.

items.title: Do not resend immediately
items.description: Wait for normal crawling and indexing signals instead of burning rate limits.

sections.title: If the page is still not indexed
paragraphs: Check robots directives, canonical tags, content quality, HTTP status, internal links, and the search engine's webmaster tools.

sections.title: Confirming crawl and indexing
paragraphs: HTTP 200 confirms protocol receipt and ownership verification only. Crawling and ranking still depend on normal search quality signals, robots.txt permissions, canonical tags, and server availability.

items.title: Inspect Bing Webmaster Tools
items.description: Open the IndexNow report in Bing Webmaster Tools to verify submitted URL counts and crawl timestamps.

items.title: Check live HTTP status
items.description: Ensure submitted URLs return HTTP 200 (or 404/410 for intentionally removed pages) without redirect chains.

items.title: Audit robots and canonicals
items.description: Verify no unintended noindex meta tag, X-Robots-Tag header, or cross-page canonical prevents indexing.

title: IndexNow 202: Accepted
description: Why IndexNow returns HTTP 202 while key validation is pending and when to retry.
summary: The request was received, but ownership validation has not finished.

sections.title: Meaning
paragraphs: The endpoint received a valid-looking request and will validate the key asynchronously. A 202 is not an error.

items.title: Key file
items.description: Confirm the file is public, returns 200, and contains only the exact key.

items.title: Host consistency
items.description: The host, keyLocation hostname, and every submitted URL hostname must match.

sections.title: Retry policy
paragraphs: Do not loop on 202. Verify the key once, then wait before submitting only genuinely changed URLs.

sections.title: How to verify while validation is pending
paragraphs: A 202 response commonly appears on a site's first submission, after rotating a key, or when CDN edge caches have not yet propagated the key file globally.
sections.code:
curl -iL "https://www.example.com/your-key.txt"
# Expected:
# HTTP/2 200
# content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
# Body equals the exact key with no HTML wrapper or BOM

items.title: Wait before re-sending
items.description: Allow asynchronous validation to complete rather than sending repeated identical batches.

items.title: Check CDN and origin logs
items.description: Look for Bingbot or IndexNow verifier requests to /<key>.txt returning 200.

title: IndexNow 400: Bad Request
description: Diagnose malformed IndexNow payloads, invalid fields, and unsupported request shapes.
summary: The request syntax or one of its required fields is invalid.

items.title: Malformed JSON
items.description: The body is not valid JSON or Content-Type is not application/json.

items.title: Missing fields
items.description: host, key, keyLocation, or urlList is absent or has the wrong type.

items.title: Invalid key
items.description: The key is outside the 8–128 character range or contains unsupported characters.

sections.title: Diagnosis
paragraphs: Generate the request from a known-good payload, inspect the exact outgoing body, and validate it before sending.

sections.title: Retry policy
paragraphs: A retry with the same body will fail again. Correct the payload first.

sections.title: Minimal valid payload schema
paragraphs: Verify your serialized request body matches the required field names and types exactly. Common 400 triggers include passing a string instead of an array for urlList, sending an empty urlList, or exceeding 10,000 URLs in one request.

items.title: Key charset and length
items.description: Must be 8 to 128 characters using only a–z, A–Z, 0–9, and hyphens (-).

items.title: URL encoding
items.description: Percent-encode spaces and non-ASCII characters in urlList entries according to RFC 3986.

title: IndexNow 403: Key Not Valid
description: Fix IndexNow ownership verification failures caused by key-file content, redirects, WAF rules, or host mismatch.
summary: The search engine could not validate the key against the submitted host.

items.title: Wrong response body
items.description: Whitespace, HTML, a UTF-8 BOM, or another key is present in the file.

items.title: Off-host redirect
items.description: The key URL redirects to a different hostname.

items.title: Crawler blocked
items.description: Authentication, WAF, bot protection, or geo rules block the external fetch.

sections.title: Diagnosis
paragraphs: Open the key checker, enter the exact host and key, and inspect the final URL, response type, byte content, and redirect behavior.

sections.title: Fix and retry
paragraphs: Deploy a plain text file on the same hostname, purge CDN caches, verify it from the public internet, then retry one small batch.

sections.title: Command-line key file diagnostic
paragraphs: Inspect both the HTTP status chain and raw bytes of the key file from outside your private network. Hidden UTF-8 BOM bytes (ef bb bf), trailing HTML from a soft-404 catch-all route, or a redirect from apex to www frequently cause 403 rejections.
sections.code:
curl -sS -D - "https://www.example.com/your-key.txt" | head -n 20
# Check for hidden BOM or extra characters:
curl -sS "https://www.example.com/your-key.txt" | xxd

items.title: Cloudflare / WAF bot fight mode
items.description: Add an allow rule for /<key>.txt so managed challenges do not return an HTML interstitial to the verifier.

items.title: SPA / Next.js middleware catch-all
items.description: Exclude static .txt files from i18n redirects and authentication middleware so the key file returns plain text with HTTP 200.

title: IndexNow 422: Unprocessable Entity
description: Resolve IndexNow host, keyLocation, and URL-list consistency errors.
summary: The payload is readable, but its URLs or ownership fields are inconsistent.

items.title: Mixed hosts
items.description: The urlList contains more than one hostname.

items.title: Host mismatch
items.description: The host field differs from the URL hostname, including www versus apex.

items.title: Invalid key location
items.description: keyLocation belongs to another hostname or does not correspond to the key.

sections.title: Diagnosis
paragraphs: Normalize the URL list, group it by exact hostname, and generate one request per group.

sections.title: Retry policy
paragraphs: Correct the host boundaries before retrying. Splitting by protocol is unnecessary, but splitting by hostname is mandatory.

sections.title: Common host-boundary mismatches
paragraphs: IndexNow treats each hostname (including subdomains and www) as a separate ownership boundary. Even a single mismatched URL inside a 5,000-URL batch causes the entire request to fail with 422.

items.title: Apex vs. www
items.description: host: example.com cannot submit https://www.example.com/page — split them into two batches.

items.title: Subdomains and staging hosts
items.description: Filter out preview, staging, or blog.example.com URLs when submitting for www.example.com.

items.title: Subdirectory keyLocation scope
items.description: If keyLocation is placed in a subdirectory such as /blog/key.txt, it can only authorize URLs under /blog/.

title: IndexNow 429: Too Many Requests
description: Reduce IndexNow request volume with deduplication, sitemap diffs, batching, and backoff.
summary: The endpoint is rate limiting the host or client.

sections.title: Why it happens
paragraphs: Repeated full-sitemap submissions, duplicate URLs, parallel retries, and multiple integrations can exceed the endpoint's current allowance.

items.title: Submit changes only
items.description: Compare sitemap snapshots and send added or genuinely modified URLs.

items.title: Coordinate publishers
items.description: Ensure the CMS plugin, deploy hook, and manual tool do not submit the same change.

items.title: Back off
items.description: Use exponential backoff with jitter and cap retries.

sections.title: Do not
paragraphs: Do not rotate keys, change IP addresses, or retry continuously. Those actions do not fix the underlying request volume.

sections.title: Safe retry and backoff pattern
paragraphs: Honor Retry-After headers when present and switch from per-edit single-URL pings to scheduled batched submissions (for example, one batch every 5–15 minutes or once per production deployment).
sections.code:
const delayMs = Math.min(60_000, 1000 * 2 ** attempt) + Math.floor(Math.random() * 500);
await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs));

items.title: Deduplicate URLs before queuing
items.description: Normalize query strings and trailing slashes so the same canonical page is not submitted multiple times.

items.title: Avoid full-site re-pings
items.description: Use sitemap diffing to extract only URLs whose content or lastmod genuinely changed.

title: IndexNow for WordPress
description: Configure one WordPress IndexNow publisher, verify its key file, and prevent duplicate submissions.
summary: Use a maintained plugin, validate ownership, and avoid overlapping SEO plugins.

sections.title: Choose one publisher
paragraphs: Use one maintained plugin that explicitly supports IndexNow. Disable duplicate IndexNow features in other SEO or caching plugins.

items.title: Enable IndexNow
items.description: Turn on the integration and let the plugin generate or accept a key.

items.title: Verify the key file
items.description: Confirm the public file is served by WordPress or the web root without authentication.

items.title: Test one update
items.description: Publish or update one page, then inspect the plugin log and endpoint response.

sections.title: Operational checks
paragraphs: After domain changes, CDN migrations, or security-plugin updates, recheck the key file before debugging submissions.

sections.title: Avoiding plugin conflicts
paragraphs: Many WordPress SEO suites (Yoast SEO, Rank Math, AIOSEO) and caching layers (Cloudflare Crawler Hints) include built-in IndexNow toggles. Running multiple publishers simultaneously causes duplicate submissions, mismatched keys, and 429 rate limiting.

items.title: Keep one active publisher
items.description: Disable IndexNow in secondary SEO plugins and keep either the official IndexNow plugin or a single SEO suite enabled.

items.title: Verify static vs. virtual key files
items.description: If security plugins block virtual rewrite rules, place a physical <key>.txt file in the WordPress document root.

items.title: Exclude non-indexable post types
items.description: Avoid notifying draft previews, attachment pages, or noindex tag archives.

title: IndexNow with Next.js
description: Publish an IndexNow key in Next.js and submit changed URLs from a trusted server-side deploy hook.
summary: Serve the key from public/, then submit changed URLs from server-only code.

sections.title: Publish the key
paragraphs: Place KEY.txt in public/ so the deployed site serves it from the hostname root. Keep the submission secret in server-only environment configuration, not client bundles.

sections.title: Submit from trusted code

items.title: Calculate changes
items.description: Compare the previous and current sitemap or use CMS webhook payloads.

items.title: Group by host
items.description: Build one payload for each exact hostname.

items.title: Log safely
items.description: Record status and counts, never the key or private draft URLs.

sections.title: Middleware and i18n exclusions
paragraphs: In Next.js App Router projects using next-intl or custom auth middleware, ensure your matcher skips static .txt files in public/ so https://example.com/<key>.txt serves directly without locale prefixes or redirects.

items.title: Diff the live sitemap after deploy
items.description: Compare the pre-deploy and post-deploy sitemap.xml to collect only added or modified URLs.

items.title: Run server-side after health check
items.description: Trigger the POST request only after the new deployment passes smoke checks so crawlers fetch fresh pages.

title: IndexNow with Cloudflare Workers
description: Send IndexNow updates from a Cloudflare Worker using Secrets, waitUntil, and bounded retry behavior.
summary: Keep the key in a Secret and submit publish events without delaying the response.

sections.title: Store configuration safely
paragraphs: Bind the key as a Worker Secret. Keep host and keyLocation in environment configuration, and never return the key from an HTTP response.

sections.title: Submit in the background

items.title: Authenticate the trigger
items.description: Verify the CMS webhook signature or protect the endpoint with service authentication.

items.title: Bound the batch
items.description: Validate host consistency and enforce the 10,000 URL maximum.

items.title: Retry selectively
items.description: Retry network failures and 429 responses with backoff, not permanent 400-series errors.

sections.title: Serving the key file from the Worker
paragraphs: If your domain routes all traffic through Cloudflare Workers, you can serve the ownership key file directly from the Worker with an explicit text/plain header and cache control, avoiding origin round-trips.

sections.title: Queueing and deduplication at the edge

items.title: Batch with Cloudflare Queues or Cron Triggers
items.description: Buffer publish webhooks and flush grouped same-host batches every few minutes to avoid 429 throttling.

items.title: Disable Bot Fight challenges on the key path
items.description: Ensure WAF rules allow automated GET requests to /<key>.txt without JavaScript challenges.
